source.section: PDF page 9, Line 29 (If you became 59 1/2 during 2025, enter only the amount you received after you became 59 1/2); Form IT-201 line 29; Form IT-201 lines 19, 24, 32-39 (PDF pages 2-3); IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34 standard deduction table), PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39, rate schedule)

worked: Single, born 1966-03-01: 59 at December 31, 2025, and 59 1/2 on September 1, 2025. Wages 80,000 and IRA distributions 18,000. The booklet allows only the IRA amount received after September 1, 2025; the projection treats reaching 59 1/2 in the year as qualifying for the whole year's 18,000 (accepted approximation; if all 18,000 came before September 1 the booklet's exclusion would be 0 and its tax 18,000 x 5.5% = 990.00 higher). Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 98,000.00. Federal taxable income = 98,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 82,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtraction: line 29 exclusion as the projection applies it (59 1/2 reached in 2025 counts for the whole year): IRA 18,000, under 20,000 18,000.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 18,000.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 98,000.00 - 18,000.00 = 80,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (single, PDF page 11 table) 8,000.00; line 35 = 80,000.00 - 8,000.00 = 72,000.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 72,000.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, single) on 72,000.00: 8,500.00 x 4% = 340.00; 3,200.00 x 4.5% = 144.00; 2,200.00 x 5.25% = 115.50; 58,100.00 x 5.5% = 3,195.50; schedule tax = 3,795.00 (the printed schedule, with its whole-dollar base 600 at 13,900, gives 3,795.50; this case uses the bands as numbers). NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 3,795.00. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 3,795.00.
accepted_approximations: The exclusion's age test is applied as reaching 59 1/2 in the year; the booklet counts, in the year a person reaches 59 1/2, only income received after that date.
